policy.clock: Automatic mode reads original Universe/Sector solar orientation in a campaign, including tidal lock. Maps without a sector use state.tick with a decorative simulated-time cycle. An explicit visual-cycle setting allows the same cosmetic cycle on any map. Neither mode writes simulation clocks, ambientLight, solar power or other game rules.
policy.sky: Original procedural ray-based atmosphere, sun, stars and stylized companion planet; ray basis follows full quaternion camera including roll. Companion identity and palette use native Serpulo/Erekir data. Its enlarged angular size and always-above-horizon placement are artistic, not an astronomical orbit simulation.
policy.background: A cached deterministic skirt and mountain rings outside the exact rectangular map boundary. Decorative only: never add tiles, collision, build targets, resources or enemies. Current map dimensions determine their extent; palette follows the planet.
policy.visibility: No distance fog conceals playable terrain. Native discovery and entity visibility remain renderer responsibilities. Sky and background render into the renderer's existing depth framebuffer, before world geometry.
policy.testing: A preview phase override is accepted only when fpv.smoke is explicitly true; it does not alter native time. Runtime checks compare game-clock changes and confirm freeze at0 percent plus day/night screenshots.
policy.farPlane: farPlane(Camera3D) preserves map-diagonal baseline and extends to camera-to-map-center distance plus a sphere enclosing all decorative mountain rings, with margin. Camera altitude and chase displacement are included, so small maps remain visible from720 tiles above. Ray-based sky remains independent of depth distance.

acceptance.criterion: Camera far plane covers the map diagonal and background; atmospheric distance fade is absent from world geometry.
Read-only time follows the native campaign or map clock and holds during Build0 pause; explicit preview leaves game state untouched.
Actual framebuffer captures show native textured map, continuous distant mountain backdrop, day/night sky, stars and other planet; no GL errors.
